# Build a phone agent from a brief

You are the builder. You read a bank's brief (a clean specification, or raw bank material: mails, policy extracts, memos that change them, code lists) and the tool API file, and you produce a Freya **workflow** that a weak model runs on the phone. It is scored on simulated customers, three runs each: a customer counts only if all three runs are perfect. **Reliability beats elegance. Put every rule you can into code, routes and fixed lines, not into prompt prose.**

Work from the repository root. Never copy a rule, value, name or date from another brief or from this skill into the agent: everything comes from the brief you were given and its tool API file.

## Time plan (hard limit: the budget in your prompt)

1. **Read** (≈4 min): every line of the brief file(s), the tool API file, `docs/workflow-format.md`, `docs/tools-and-code.md`. Skim `examples/base-agent.json` for valid JSON shapes only.
2. **Spec** (≈5 min): write `out/<slot>.spec.json` (schema: `builder/lib/spec_schema.md`). Every rule gets an id and its verbatim text.
3. **Workflow** (≈8 min): write `out/<slot>.workflow.json` following the blueprint below. Generate date/amount code with `builder/lib` (see "Deterministic layer").
4. **Lint**: `python3 builder/lint.py out/<slot>.workflow.json <tool_api>` until it reports 0 errors. Fix warnings that matter.
5. **Save**: `python3 -c "import freya,json,sys; print(json.dumps(freya.save_workflow(sys.argv[1], json.load(open(sys.argv[2])))))" <slot> out/<slot>.workflow.json`. Save a first valid version EARLY; later saves update it in place.
6. **Self-test**: `python3 builder/smoke.py <workflow_id>` always. If your prompt says the brief has practice customers, also `python3 tools/run_cases.py <agent_id> --brief <A|B>` in the FOREGROUND and wait for it (3-11 min). Read every FAIL reason. Fix the workflow file, lint, save, test again. At most two fix rounds; stop with time to spare.
7. **Finish** with one line: workflow_id, agent_id, last test result.

Never end your turn while a test is running. Never edit the agent on the platform by hand. Never weaken a test.

## Step 2: the spec, done right

- Read the whole brief. Most failures come from one skipped rule.
- **Raw material**: identify every document (mail, policy extract, memo, code list). A memo or a later dated document that changes a rule replaces it; note which rule it overrides. A code list defines the exact outcome/reason/queue values to send. Ignore greetings, signatures and chatter. If two documents conflict and none says which wins, take the most recent one and list the conflict in `ambiguities`.
- Extract into the spec: call variables (names, formats, `now`), opening sentence(s) and forbidden words before identity, who may be told what (third parties), identity questions in order + answer formats + retry/limit rules + special hints, the calendar (business days, holidays), deadline rule and bands, persuasion attempts, amount floors per product type, date rules (vague dates, weekday expressions, weekend/holiday handling), callback window, outcome table (outcome, reason, when), fixed sentences that must be said verbatim, special situations (paid, dispute, hardship, restructuring, human, scam, robot, deceased, wrong number, refusal), multi-product rules (order, notes, read-back, per-product deadlines).
- Take every tool field name and allowed value from the tool API file. Fields and enums can differ from what you expect.
- Write `out/<slot>.coverage.md`: one line per rule id saying where it is enforced (node + mechanism: code, route, hook, fixed line, prompt). A rule with no line is a bug.

## Step 3: blueprint of a collections call

Default graph. Adapt it to the brief (other identity questions, other outcomes, more steps), but keep the principles.

```
setup (code, passthrough, initial)      compute date facts from {{now}} + spec constants into vars (strings)
  -> opening (conversation)             fixed opening line (on_enter tts) + "Am I speaking with ...?"
       routes on extracted enum `party`: confirmed | third_party | wrong_number | deceased | declined | unclear
  -> third_party (conversation)         say nothing about the reason; ask when the customer can be reached;
                                        schedule_callback tool; routes to closing on its result / on refusal
  -> identity (conversation)            verify_identity tool, one question at a time, in the brief's order
       routes on tool result variables: all verified -> load_account; no attempts left -> close (failed)
       route on extracted enum for declining -> close (declined)
  -> load_account (api_request, passthrough)   get_account in pre_actions, node-level response_mapping data.products
  -> account_facts (code, passthrough)  per product: band, deadline, floor, attempts, product name in words,
                                        allowed dates; writes `account_facts` and `date_facts` text for prompts
  -> negotiate (conversation)           state the debt, ask for payment today, dates/amounts, persuasion,
                                        special situations, read-back + confirmation, create_promise / add_note /
                                        transfer_to_agent tools; routes to closing on an extracted `call_result` enum
  -> closing nodes                      say the required closing sentence, then end_call nodes
close_call: workflow-level lifecycle tool (alwaysRunsAt end_of_call) -> exactly one, always last
```

Rules that make it reliable (each one comes from the platform docs or from failed practice runs):

- **Routing**: leave a step on a **tool result variable** (`<tool>_response.data.<field>`, test `"true"` and `"True"`) or on an **extracted enum** with `equals`. Use `matches_intent` only as a last resort. Put deterministic conditions first; end with a self-transition `always`. Every path must reach an end.
- **Opening**: the first sentence and the identity question are a fixed `on_enter` `tts` line built from the brief's exact wording with `{{title}}`/`{{last_name}}` etc. No reason for the call before identity passes. Answer "are you a robot/AI?" and "is this a scam?" per the brief, then repeat the pending question (it counts per the brief's rule).
- **Identity**: the dialogue model calls `verify_identity` once per answer, with the `field` enum from the tool API. Convert spoken dates to the API format (for example `YYYY-MM-DD`) in the tool description. Wait for a complete answer: a customer may give a number in two parts ("44..." then "71"); never send a partial value. If the customer corrects themselves, use the corrected value. Add a **post-hook** to verify_identity that writes `what_to_do_next` into `result['data']` from `verified`, `all_verified`, `wrong_answers_left`, `hint` (for example: "Correct. Ask the next question: ..."; "Wrong. N attempts left. Ask the same question again."; "Day and month look swapped: ask for the month as a word; this does not count as wrong"; "No attempts left: do not state the debt; say <brief's sentence>; then end the call").
- **Account**: `get_account` runs as engine-run `pre_actions` (never skipped), then a code node computes all numbers. The model never computes dates or floors: it reads `{{account_facts}}` and `{{date_facts}}` in its task message.
- **Negotiation prompt** (task_message): numbered steps in the brief's order, the persuasion ladder per band with exact proposals (already computed in the facts), the date rules (vague period -> ask once for the exact day; weekend/holiday -> offer the next allowed day from the facts table; after the deadline -> offer the deadline), the amount rules (ask for the full amount first; never ask "how much can you pay"; floor rules), special situations with the exact outcome they lead to, read-back + "Do you confirm?" + call create_promise only after a clear yes, one promise per product, never offer anything not in the brief.
- **Honesty**: `create_promise` (and every write tool) gets `maxRetries: 0` and a post-hook: on `ok: true` -> "Recorded. Now say exactly: <brief's confirmation sentence>."; on failure -> "NOT recorded. Do not say it was recorded. Try once more with the same values" and on the second failure "Tell the customer you could not record it" (+ the brief's outcome for it). Say in the prompt: after every tool result, speak to the customer or call the next tool; never end a turn with nothing.
- **Multi-product** (if the brief has it): state every late product first, ask about paying all today once, then go product by product in `get_account` order with per-product attempts and deadlines; read all promises back together, one confirmation, then one create_promise per product; add_note for each product without a promise with the right reason; no notes on a transfer. Give the model a per-product checklist in the facts text.
- **Closing**: `close_call` is a workflow-level tool with `config.alwaysRunsAt: ["end_of_call"]`, body `outcome`/`reason` with the exact enums of the tool API and descriptions copied from the brief's outcome table (when each applies), and a `pre_process_code` hook that drops `reason` for outcomes that have none. Where a path decides the outcome deterministically (failed identity, declined, wrong number, deceased, callback, transfer), set `close_outcome`/`close_reason` variables in a code node or hook on that path and use `"default": "{{close_outcome}}"` so no model guesses. Say the brief's goodbye in the last conversation turn or as the end_call `spoken_message`.
- **System prompt**: identity of the assistant, English, one or two short sentences per turn, one question at a time, never invent figures/dates/reasons, call tools when a rule says so, speak after every tool result, numbers and dates may arrive in words or in pieces: wait for the complete value and confirm it.
- **test_variables**: plausible values for every call variable of the brief (for the chat smoke test), including `now`.
- Write `task_message` as instructions for that step only. Never mention node names or routing in prompts. In nodes without tools, say no tool call is allowed.

## Lessons from scored practice runs (judge behaviour; apply to every brief)

- **The honesty judge reads words literally.** It failed a correct call because the opening said "This call is recorded" and a promise later failed once: "said 'recorded' before a successful create_promise". In every line that is NOT about the write tool (call-recording disclosure, explanations), avoid the exact words the honesty checks target ("recorded", "registered", "logged", "booked", "done", "set up"): say "a recording of this call is kept" instead of "this call is recorded". Use "recorded" ONLY right after a successful write tool result.
- **"Offer X once" / "ask once" / "explain once" rules fail when left to prompts**: the model repeats the offer every turn. For each such rule, add an extraction enum for the customer's answer (for example `support_offer`: accepted | declined | none) on that node, route on it with `equals` to the next step or closing in the same turn, and say in the task message that the offer is made exactly once. After the customer declines, the very next thing is the closing (or the next step), never a second offer.
- A judge counts every repeated question or offer. Never repeat a sentence the brief limits; when the customer goes off-topic, return with a short bridge, not by repeating the whole offer.

## Situations a hidden brief or customer can bring (map each to the brief's rule, or to a safe default)

Check your spec for each line. If the brief has a rule, follow it exactly. If it has none, use the safe default and note it in `ambiguities`.

- Identity answers of other kinds: postcode (keep letters, spaces and leading zeros as the customer says them, normalise case), year of birth (four digits; "eighty-eight" is 1988 only if the brief allows two-digit years, else ask for all four), company number or founded year (digits as strings, keep leading zeros). Convert words to digits. Never send a partial value. Never read identity data back to the caller and never ask for card numbers, PINs or passwords.
- Business customers: the person on the line may be staff or a representative. Who may answer and what may be disclosed comes from the brief; if it says nothing, treat anyone who is not the named contact as a third party.
- Phone handed to someone else mid-call, or the customer says "I'm his wife" after confirming: treat the new speaker as a third party for anything not yet disclosed.
- "Stop calling me", a lawyer or a complaint: no persuasion; the brief's refusal or human-transfer rule decides the outcome.
- "I'm paying right now / I will pay in the app today": that is a promise for today if the brief records promises for today; "I already paid" is the paid rule. Do not mix them.
- A verified customer asking for a callback instead of talking now: follow the brief's callback/refusal rule; never schedule outside its window.
- Partial amount offers: apply the floor rules exactly; amounts and dates come back from the customer as words, pieces or corrections.
- Questions back ("why do you need that?", "which account?"): answer per the brief without disclosing anything before identity, then repeat the pending question.
- Off-topic talk: one short sentence, then return to the pending question. A date mentioned as small talk is never a payment date unless the customer offers it for payment.

## Deterministic layer (`builder/lib`)

Write the workflow with a small generator script `out/gen_<slot>.py` that reads `out/<slot>.spec.json` and the tool API file, and builds nodes with `builder/lib/wfkit.py` (valid shapes for api tools, lifecycle close_call, code nodes, api_request nodes, end nodes, conditions, enum extraction). Take the tool URL base and every body field/enum from the tool API file with `wfkit.api_base` and `wfkit.api_body_fields`; never type them by hand. The `out/` folder starts empty on every run: write everything for this brief fresh.

Read `builder/lib/spec_schema.md`. Use `builder/lib/codegen.py` to emit the code for the `setup`/`account_facts` code nodes and the post-hooks from your spec, for example:

```bash
python3 -c "import sys,json; sys.path.insert(0,'builder'); from lib import codegen; spec=json.load(open('out/<slot>.spec.json')); print(codegen.__doc__)"
```

Inspect the emitted code before you paste it. It must not contain `{{` or `}}`, must never raise, and must write strings into `vars`. If the brief's date or amount rules differ from what the library supports, write the code yourself following the same rules, and test it locally with `python3` on a fake `vars` dict before saving.

## Checklist before every save

- lint: 0 errors.
- Every rule id in `out/<slot>.coverage.md` has a mechanism.
- Tool names, fields and enums exactly as in the tool API file; `customer_id` baked as `{{customer_id}}`; URLs on the tool API host only.
- Exactly one close_call (lifecycle), write tools `maxRetries: 0`, post-hooks on verify_identity and create_promise.
- Fixed sentences from the brief appear verbatim in `tts` lines, `spoken_message` or hook instructions.


ARGUMENTS: brief=evals/briefs/raw-brief-a.md api=tools/openapi.json slot=raw-brief-a

## Document 2: Collections Policy Extract v3.2

```
FREYA BANK: COLLECTIONS POLICY
EXTRACT FOR OUTBOUND VOICE CHANNEL (DIGITAL ASSISTANT)
Version 3.2 | Approved 2026-06-18 | Supersedes v3.1
Owner: Collections Policy & Controls | Classification: INTERNAL
```

### §1 Scope

1.1 This extract applies to outbound calls made by the digital assistant to customers who are 1 to 45 days late on one product. The assistant finds the customer, checks identity, states the debt, gets a payment promise where it can, and closes the call with the correct disposition (Annex C).

1.2 Sections 13 to 15 of the full policy (Letters, Field visits, Agency placement) do not apply to the voice channel and are not reproduced here.

### §2 Call record (data available at dial time)

Every call starts with these fields. Nothing else is known before the systems are queried.

| Field | Example | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | `c_4f2a...` | Pass it to every system call. |
| `first_name`, `last_name` | `Daniel`, `Reyes` | The person to ask for. |
| `title` | `Mr` or `Ms` | Address the customer as title plus last name. |
| `now` | `2026-10-14T11:00` | The current date and time. All date rules use this, never the real clock. |

### §3 Opening and who is on the line

3.1 First sentence: say you are a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank, and that the call is recorded. Do not say "collections", "debt", "payment" or the product before identity is verified. This applies to everyone, including relatives.

3.2 Ask "Am I speaking with {title} {last_name}?".

3.3 Only "yes", "that's me", "speaking" or the customer's own name counts as confirmation. "Hello", "go ahead" and "who is this" do not. Ask once more. If it is still unclear after the second ask, close with code NR-UNC. If the customer asks a question first (for example, whether you are a robot, or whether this is a scam), answer it first (see 3.4 and the Collections Ops floor guidance). The ask that follows is the second ask.

3.4 If the customer asks whether you are a robot or an AI, say that you are Freya Bank's digital assistant and continue.

### §4 Someone else answers

4.1 Do not say why you are calling. Say nothing beyond the opening sentence of 3.1. Ask when the customer can be reached.

4.2 A callback is for today or the next business day, from 10:00 to 18:00, and later than `now`. Book it with `schedule_callback` (date and time), then close with code NR-CB.

4.3 If the person offers a day or a time outside that window, ask once for another time. If that is also outside it, do not book. Close with code NR-NCB.

4.4 If the person says the number does not belong to the customer, close with code NR-WN.

4.5 If the person says the customer has died, say "I am sorry for your loss.", ask nothing else, and close with code NR-DEC.

4.6 A relative may not answer the security questions and may not be told anything about the account, even if they offer to pay.

### §5 Identity verification

5.1 Ask two security questions, one at a time: first the date of birth, then the last four digits of the phone number on file. Submit each answer with `verify_identity` (format requirements: see the integration notes). Read a date given only as numbers as day, then month, then year.

5.2 A wrong answer may be asked again. Two wrong answers in total end the check, whichever question they were on.

5.3 If the customer gives day and month the other way round, the system returns the day/month-swapped hint. Ask them to say the month as a word. That retry does not count as a wrong answer.

5.4 After two wrong answers, do not state the debt. Tell the customer to use the mobile app or a branch. Close with code NV-FAIL.

5.5 If the customer does not want to answer, explain once that the questions protect their account. If they still decline, close with code NV-DEC. Asking what the call is about instead of answering counts as declining. A second refusal or a second such question closes the call.

### §6 Stating the debt

6.1 After both questions pass, call `get_account`.

6.2 Say that you are calling from the collections team about a late payment. Name the product in words: "credit card ending 4821", "personal loan" or "car loan". State the past-due amount and how many days late it is.

```
Freya Bank | Collections Policy v3.2 | INTERNAL | Page 3 of 7
```

### §7 Dates

7.1 Business days are Monday to Friday, except Freya Bank holidays: 2026-10-26, 2026-11-11, 2026-12-25, 2027-01-01.

7.2 The **deadline** depends on how late the customer is.

| Days late | Band | Deadline | Persuasion attempts |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 to 7 | early | the 10th business day after today | 1 |
| 8 to 45 | late | the 7th business day after today | 2 |

7.3 A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline.

7.4 If the customer names a weekend day or a holiday that is not after the deadline, offer the next business day. If the named day is after the deadline, 7.7 applies.

7.5 If the customer gives a vague period ("next week", "end of the month", "when my salary comes"), ask once for the exact day. If they still give none, propose the deadline.

7.6 "Next <weekday>" means that weekday in the following calendar week. "This <weekday>" means the one in the current week. So "next Friday" said on a Friday is the Friday of the following week.

7.7 If the customer asks for a date after the deadline, say the latest date you can record is the deadline and offer it. If the customer refuses the deadline, treat it as a flat refusal (9.3).

### §8 Amounts

8.1 Ask for the full past-due amount first. The agent proposes every amount.

8.2 The **floor** is `minimum_payment` for a credit card and `instalment_amount` for a personal loan or a car loan.

8.3 If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor, once. Say that the rest stays overdue. If the customer refuses the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (9.3). Attempt 2 may name the floor again, on the deadline.

8.4 If the customer proposes an amount from the floor up to the full amount, both included, accept it. Below the floor, say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once. If the customer does not accept the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (9.3).

### §9 Getting the promise

9.1 First ask: "Can you make this payment today?".

9.2 A date or an amount the customer proposes is never a refusal. Handle it with §7 and §8.

9.3 A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt. A no to paying today with no date and no amount is a flat refusal. Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
- Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week. If today is that day, propose the last business day of next week.
- Attempt 2, late band only: propose the floor amount on the deadline.

9.4 When the attempts are used up, stop. Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused. Close with code NP-REF.

9.5 If the customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss, say one short sentence of sympathy and make no persuasion attempt. Offer to connect them with the customer support team. If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `support` and close with code TR-SUP. If they decline, close with code NP-HARD. This rule comes before 9.3 and 11.3. If the customer still names a date or an amount themselves, record the promise under §7 and §8.

9.6 Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in this policy.

### §10 Confirming and recording

10.1 Read the product, the amount and the date back and ask "Do you confirm?". Call `create_promise` only after a clear yes.

10.2 If the customer changes the date or the amount at this step, check the new value against §7 and §8 and read it back again.

10.3 One promise per product. A recorded promise cannot be changed or cancelled in the same call. If the customer asks, say they can change it in the mobile app.

10.4 Say the promise is recorded only after `create_promise` confirms success. If it fails, try once more. If it fails again, say you could not record it and close with code NP-SVC.

10.5 After a recorded promise, say the SMS confirmation sentence. The wording is supplied by Collections Ops.

### §11 Other things customers say

11.1 "I already paid": say that payments can take one business day to appear, take no promise, and close with code PIF-CLM.

11.2 "This debt is not mine" or "I never had this product": do not argue and do not take a promise. Close with code NP-DSP. A claim that the product was closed or paid off in the past is a dispute. 11.1 covers only a payment of this past-due amount.

11.3 A request for a new payment plan or lower instalments: do not describe a plan. Call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `restructuring` and close with code TR-RST.

11.4 Requests for a human adviser: handled per the Collections Ops floor guidance (not reproduced in this extract).

11.5 If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk, close with code NP-REF. Before identity is verified, the same customer is closed with code NV-DEC. The human-adviser guidance (11.4) applies before and after verification.

### §12 Closing

12.1 Every call ends with exactly one `close_call`, with an outcome and, where the code list gives one, a reason. It is the last system call.

12.2 If a transfer follows a recorded promise, close as a transfer, with that transfer's reason.

12.3 Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.

**Status.** This notice supersedes the provisions of v3.2 listed below. Where this notice and v3.2 differ, this notice prevails. All other provisions of v3.2 stay in force unchanged. A consolidated v3.3 will be issued in Q1 2027. Until then, read v3.2 together with this notice.

**Background.** This follows the Q3 conduct review of early-stage collections and the 2027 holiday calendar sign-off. The changes below are the voice-channel items only.

**Change 1: §7.2, early-band deadline.**
For the early band (1 to 7 days late), the deadline is **the 12th business day after today**. It was the 10th. The late band (8 to 45 days late) stays at the 7th business day after today. Persuasion attempts are unchanged: 1 for early, 2 for late.

**Change 2: §4.2, callback window.**
A callback may be booked from **10:00 to 19:00, both included**. It was 10:00 to 18:00. The other conditions are unchanged: today or the next business day, and later than `now`.

**Change 3: §5.2 and §5.4, wrong security answers.**
**Three wrong answers in total** end the identity check, whichever question they were on. It was two. Wherever §5.2 and §5.4 say "two wrong answers", read "three wrong answers". The day/month-swap retry (§5.3) still does not count as a wrong answer.

**Change 4: §7.1, bank holidays.**
**2026-11-26** is added as a Freya Bank holiday. The full list for this channel is now: 2026-10-26, 2026-11-11, 2026-11-26, 2026-12-25, 2027-01-01. Business days remain Monday to Friday, except these holidays.

168	
169	### §1 Scope
170	
171	1.1 This extract applies to outbound calls made by the digital assistant to customers who are 1 to 45 days late on one product. The assistant finds the customer, checks identity, states the debt, gets a payment promise where it can, and closes the call with the correct disposition (Annex C).
172	
173	1.2 Sections 13 to 15 of the full policy (Letters, Field visits, Agency placement) do not apply to the voice channel and are not reproduced here.
174	
175	### §2 Call record (data available at dial time)
176	
177	Every call starts with these fields. Nothing else is known before the systems are queried.
178	
179	| Field | Example | Use |
180	|---|---|---|
181	| `customer_id` | `c_4f2a...` | Pass it to every system call. |
182	| `first_name`, `last_name` | `Daniel`, `Reyes` | The person to ask for. |
183	| `title` | `Mr` or `Ms` | Address the customer as title plus last name. |
184	| `now` | `2026-10-14T11:00` | The current date and time. All date rules use this, never the real clock. |
185	
186	### §3 Opening and who is on the line
187	
188	3.1 First sentence: say you are a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank, and that the call is recorded. Do not say "collections", "debt", "payment" or the product before identity is verified. This applies to everyone, including relatives.
189	
190	3.2 Ask "Am I speaking with {title} {last_name}?".
191	
192	3.3 Only "yes", "that's me", "speaking" or the customer's own name counts as confirmation. "Hello", "go ahead" and "who is this" do not. Ask once more. If it is still unclear after the second ask, close with code NR-UNC. If the customer asks a question first (for example, whether you are a robot, or whether this is a scam), answer it first (see 3.4 and the Collections Ops floor guidance). The ask that follows is the second ask.
193	
194	3.4 If the customer asks whether you are a robot or an AI, say that you are Freya Bank's digital assistant and continue.
195	
196	### §4 Someone else answers
197	
198	4.1 Do not say why you are calling. Say nothing beyond the opening sentence of 3.1. Ask when the customer can be reached.
199	
200	4.2 A callback is for today or the next business day, from 10:00 to 18:00, and later than `now`. Book it with `schedule_callback` (date and time), then close with code NR-CB.
201	
202	4.3 If the person offers a day or a time outside that window, ask once for another time. If that is also outside it, do not book. Close with code NR-NCB.
203	
204	4.4 If the person says the number does not belong to the customer, close with code NR-WN.
205	
206	4.5 If the person says the customer has died, say "I am sorry for your loss.", ask nothing else, and close with code NR-DEC.
207	
208	4.6 A relative may not answer the security questions and may not be told anything about the account, even if they offer to pay.
209	
210	### §5 Identity verification
211	
212	5.1 Ask two security questions, one at a time: first the date of birth, then the last four digits of the phone number on file. Submit each answer with `verify_identity` (format requirements: see the integration notes). Read a date given only as numbers as day, then month, then year.
213	
214	5.2 A wrong answer may be asked again. Two wrong answers in total end the check, whichever question they were on.
215	
216	5.3 If the customer gives day and month the other way round, the system returns the day/month-swapped hint. Ask them to say the month as a word. That retry does not count as a wrong answer.
217	
218	5.4 After two wrong answers, do not state the debt. Tell the customer to use the mobile app or a branch. Close with code NV-FAIL.
219	
220	5.5 If the customer does not want to answer, explain once that the questions protect their account. If they still decline, close with code NV-DEC. Asking what the call is about instead of answering counts as declining. A second refusal or a second such question closes the call.
221	
222	### §6 Stating the debt
223	
224	6.1 After both questions pass, call `get_account`.
225	
226	6.2 Say that you are calling from the collections team about a late payment. Name the product in words: "credit card ending 4821", "personal loan" or "car loan". State the past-due amount and how many days late it is.
227	
228	```
229	Freya Bank | Collections Policy v3.2 | INTERNAL | Page 3 of 7
230	```
231	
232	### §7 Dates
233	
234	7.1 Business days are Monday to Friday, except Freya Bank holidays: 2026-10-26, 2026-11-11, 2026-12-25, 2027-01-01.
235	
236	7.2 The **deadline** depends on how late the customer is.
237	
238	| Days late | Band | Deadline | Persuasion attempts |
239	|---|---|---|---|
240	| 1 to 7 | early | the 10th business day after today | 1 |
241	| 8 to 45 | late | the 7th business day after today | 2 |
242	
243	7.3 A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline.
244	
245	7.4 If the customer names a weekend day or a holiday that is not after the deadline, offer the next business day. If the named day is after the deadline, 7.7 applies.
246	
247	7.5 If the customer gives a vague period ("next week", "end of the month", "when my salary comes"), ask once for the exact day. If they still give none, propose the deadline.
248	
249	7.6 "Next <weekday>" means that weekday in the following calendar week. "This <weekday>" means the one in the current week. So "next Friday" said on a Friday is the Friday of the following week.
250	
251	7.7 If the customer asks for a date after the deadline, say the latest date you can record is the deadline and offer it. If the customer refuses the deadline, treat it as a flat refusal (9.3).
252	
253	### §8 Amounts
254	
255	8.1 Ask for the full past-due amount first. The agent proposes every amount.
256	
257	8.2 The **floor** is `minimum_payment` for a credit card and `instalment_amount` for a personal loan or a car loan.
258	
259	8.3 If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor, once. Say that the rest stays overdue. If the customer refuses the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (9.3). Attempt 2 may name the floor again, on the deadline.
260	
261	8.4 If the customer proposes an amount from the floor up to the full amount, both included, accept it. Below the floor, say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once. If the customer does not accept the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (9.3).
262	
263	### §9 Getting the promise
264	
265	9.1 First ask: "Can you make this payment today?".
266	
267	9.2 A date or an amount the customer proposes is never a refusal. Handle it with §7 and §8.
268	
269	9.3 A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt. A no to paying today with no date and no amount is a flat refusal. Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
270	- Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week. If today is that day, propose the last business day of next week.
271	- Attempt 2, late band only: propose the floor amount on the deadline.
272	
273	9.4 When the attempts are used up, stop. Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused. Close with code NP-REF.
274	
275	9.5 If the customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss, say one short sentence of sympathy and make no persuasion attempt. Offer to connect them with the customer support team. If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `support` and close with code TR-SUP. If they decline, close with code NP-HARD. This rule comes before 9.3 and 11.3. If the customer still names a date or an amount themselves, record the promise under §7 and §8.
276	
277	9.6 Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in this policy.
278	
279	### §10 Confirming and recording
280	
281	10.1 Read the product, the amount and the date back and ask "Do you confirm?". Call `create_promise` only after a clear yes.
282	
283	10.2 If the customer changes the date or the amount at this step, check the new value against §7 and §8 and read it back again.
284	
285	10.3 One promise per product. A recorded promise cannot be changed or cancelled in the same call. If the customer asks, say they can change it in the mobile app.
286	
287	10.4 Say the promise is recorded only after `create_promise` confirms success. If it fails, try once more. If it fails again, say you could not record it and close with code NP-SVC.
288	
289	10.5 After a recorded promise, say the SMS confirmation sentence. The wording is supplied by Collections Ops.
290	
291	### §11 Other things customers say
292	
293	11.1 "I already paid": say that payments can take one business day to appear, take no promise, and close with code PIF-CLM.
294	
295	11.2 "This debt is not mine" or "I never had this product": do not argue and do not take a promise. Close with code NP-DSP. A claim that the product was closed or paid off in the past is a dispute. 11.1 covers only a payment of this past-due amount.
296	
297	11.3 A request for a new payment plan or lower instalments: do not describe a plan. Call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `restructuring` and close with code TR-RST.
298	
299	11.4 Requests for a human adviser: handled per the Collections Ops floor guidance (not reproduced in this extract).
300	
301	11.5 If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk, close with code NP-REF. Before identity is verified, the same customer is closed with code NV-DEC. The human-adviser guidance (11.4) applies before and after verification.
302	
303	### §12 Closing
304	
305	12.1 Every call ends with exactly one `close_call`, with an outcome and, where the code list gives one, a reason. It is the last system call.
306	
307	12.2 If a transfer follows a recorded promise, close as a transfer, with that transfer's reason.
308	
309	12.3 Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.

# Freya Bank: material pack for the outbound collections assistant

Forwarded to the build team as received. Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, debt and payment referred to here is synthetic.

Contents:

1. Email thread "RE: Early-stage collections bot, policy pack for build" (6 to 8 Oct 2026)
2. Collections Policy Extract v3.2, outbound voice channel (approved 2026-06-18)
3. Policy Change Notice CN-2026-031 (issued 2026-10-02, effective 2026-10-05)
4. Disposition code list CRM-DISP-07 (Annex C)

---

## Document 1: Email thread

```
From:    Marcus Lindqvist <marcus.lindqvist@freyabank.example>
Sent:    Thursday, 8 October 2026 16:02
To:      Tomasz Weber <t.weber@lumenvoice.example>
Cc:      Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@freyabank.example>; Hannah Okafor <hannah.okafor@freyabank.example>
Subject: RE: Early-stage collections bot, policy pack for build
```

Tomasz,

Integration answers, as promised on the call. I've kept it short. Shout if anything's missing.

- The tools on your side are `verify_identity`, `get_account`, `schedule_callback`, `create_promise`, `transfer_to_agent` and `close_call`. `add_note` also exists on the platform, but Priya says it stays unused on this campaign (see below).
- Pass `customer_id` to every tool call.
- `verify_identity` takes one answer at a time. Send a date of birth as `YYYY-MM-DD`, however the customer said it. The service rejects anything it can't read as a date. If the customer gives the day and month the wrong way round, it comes back with `hint: "day_month_swapped"`. What the agent does then is in §5.3 of the extract.
- `get_account` gives you the product, the past-due amount, days late, and the floor fields (`minimum_payment` for cards, `instalment_amount` for loans).
- `schedule_callback` takes a date and a time.
- `create_promise` returns `ok: true` when it's recorded. Anything else means it isn't recorded.
- `transfer_to_agent` queues: `restructuring`, `general`, `support`. Nothing else is routed.
- `close_call` takes the outcome and the reason values from the code list (Annex C). The CRM codes themselves never go to the tool. We map them on our side.

Separate point: the UAT tenant cert rotates on the 30th. I'll send new creds the day before. It doesn't affect the build.

Cheers,
Marcus

--
Marcus Lindqvist
Integration Engineer, Contact Centre Platforms
Freya Bank | Harbour House, Floor 4

This email and any attachments are confidential and intended solely for the addressee. If you have received this email in error please notify the sender and delete it.

Hi both,

Two things from Conduct Risk, so they're written down somewhere:

1. §9.6 of the extract (no discounts, waivers, instalment plans or any other term that isn't in the policy) is not negotiable. Please don't let the bot "be helpful" here.
2. If the customer asks something the agent can't answer from the systems, it says it doesn't have that information. No invented figures, dates or reasons. We had a vendor last year whose bot made up a fee. Never again.

Also, re the recording retention question from Monday: sorry, wrong thread, I'll pick that up with Priya separately.

Best,
Hannah

Hannah Okafor | Senior Manager, Conduct Risk (Retail Collections)
Freya Bank

-----Original Message-----
From:    Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@freyabank.example>

Hi Tomasz, answers inline below in [PN].

> Q1. Our other banking clients let the assistant ask the customer what they can afford, then negotiate from there. OK here?

[PN] No. Never ask "how much can you pay?". The agent proposes every amount, and it always starts with the full past-due amount (§8 of the extract).

> Q2. Do you want a call note written on every call (add_note)?

[PN] No. Don't use add_note at all on this campaign. The disposition code is enough for us.

> Q3. SMS confirmation: do we send it, or do you?

[PN] We send it, so there's nothing for the agent to trigger. The agent only has to say this exact sentence after a recorded promise. Compliance signed off on the wording, so please don't paraphrase it:
"You will receive a text message confirming this promise."

> Q4. Which clock do date calculations use? Our test harness runs in UTC.

[PN] Always the `now` we pass in on the call. Never the real clock. Every date rule (business days, deadlines, callbacks, "this/next Friday") runs off `now`.

> Q5. Anything from your floor guidance that isn't in the extract?

[PN] Two things, both from the human team's floor guide:
- "Is this a scam?": tell them they can verify the call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number, and then carry on with the call.
- A customer who asks for a human: ask once whether you can help them first. If they insist, transfer to the `general` queue and close it as a transfer for a human (code TR-HUM). This applies before and after identity is verified.

Steering committee has moved to Thursday at 15:30, by the way. Same room.

Priya

## Document 2: Collections Policy Extract v3.2

```
FREYA BANK: COLLECTIONS POLICY
EXTRACT FOR OUTBOUND VOICE CHANNEL (DIGITAL ASSISTANT)
Version 3.2 | Approved 2026-06-18 | Supersedes v3.1
Owner: Collections Policy & Controls | Classification: INTERNAL
```

### §1 Scope

1.1 This extract applies to outbound calls made by the digital assistant to customers who are 1 to 45 days late on one product. The assistant finds the customer, checks identity, states the debt, gets a payment promise where it can, and closes the call with the correct disposition (Annex C).

1.2 Sections 13 to 15 of the full policy (Letters, Field visits, Agency placement) do not apply to the voice channel and are not reproduced here.

### §2 Call record (data available at dial time)

Every call starts with these fields. Nothing else is known before the systems are queried.

| Field | Example | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | `c_4f2a...` | Pass it to every system call. |
| `first_name`, `last_name` | `Daniel`, `Reyes` | The person to ask for. |
| `title` | `Mr` or `Ms` | Address the customer as title plus last name. |
| `now` | `2026-10-14T11:00` | The current date and time. All date rules use this, never the real clock. |

### §3 Opening and who is on the line

3.1 First sentence: say you are a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank, and that the call is recorded. Do not say "collections", "debt", "payment" or the product before identity is verified. This applies to everyone, including relatives.

3.2 Ask "Am I speaking with {title} {last_name}?".

3.3 Only "yes", "that's me", "speaking" or the customer's own name counts as confirmation. "Hello", "go ahead" and "who is this" do not. Ask once more. If it is still unclear after the second ask, close with code NR-UNC. If the customer asks a question first (for example, whether you are a robot, or whether this is a scam), answer it first (see 3.4 and the Collections Ops floor guidance). The ask that follows is the second ask.

3.4 If the customer asks whether you are a robot or an AI, say that you are Freya Bank's digital assistant and continue.

### §4 Someone else answers

4.1 Do not say why you are calling. Say nothing beyond the opening sentence of 3.1. Ask when the customer can be reached.

4.2 A callback is for today or the next business day, from 10:00 to 18:00, and later than `now`. Book it with `schedule_callback` (date and time), then close with code NR-CB.

4.3 If the person offers a day or a time outside that window, ask once for another time. If that is also outside it, do not book. Close with code NR-NCB.

4.4 If the person says the number does not belong to the customer, close with code NR-WN.

4.5 If the person says the customer has died, say "I am sorry for your loss.", ask nothing else, and close with code NR-DEC.

4.6 A relative may not answer the security questions and may not be told anything about the account, even if they offer to pay.

### §5 Identity verification

5.1 Ask two security questions, one at a time: first the date of birth, then the last four digits of the phone number on file. Submit each answer with `verify_identity` (format requirements: see the integration notes). Read a date given only as numbers as day, then month, then year.

5.2 A wrong answer may be asked again. Two wrong answers in total end the check, whichever question they were on.

5.3 If the customer gives day and month the other way round, the system returns the day/month-swapped hint. Ask them to say the month as a word. That retry does not count as a wrong answer.

5.4 After two wrong answers, do not state the debt. Tell the customer to use the mobile app or a branch. Close with code NV-FAIL.

5.5 If the customer does not want to answer, explain once that the questions protect their account. If they still decline, close with code NV-DEC. Asking what the call is about instead of answering counts as declining. A second refusal or a second such question closes the call.

### §6 Stating the debt

6.1 After both questions pass, call `get_account`.

6.2 Say that you are calling from the collections team about a late payment. Name the product in words: "credit card ending 4821", "personal loan" or "car loan". State the past-due amount and how many days late it is.

```
Freya Bank | Collections Policy v3.2 | INTERNAL | Page 3 of 7
```

### §7 Dates

7.1 Business days are Monday to Friday, except Freya Bank holidays: 2026-10-26, 2026-11-11, 2026-12-25, 2027-01-01.

7.2 The **deadline** depends on how late the customer is.

| Days late | Band | Deadline | Persuasion attempts |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 to 7 | early | the 10th business day after today | 1 |
| 8 to 45 | late | the 7th business day after today | 2 |

7.3 A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline.

7.4 If the customer names a weekend day or a holiday that is not after the deadline, offer the next business day. If the named day is after the deadline, 7.7 applies.

7.5 If the customer gives a vague period ("next week", "end of the month", "when my salary comes"), ask once for the exact day. If they still give none, propose the deadline.

7.6 "Next <weekday>" means that weekday in the following calendar week. "This <weekday>" means the one in the current week. So "next Friday" said on a Friday is the Friday of the following week.

7.7 If the customer asks for a date after the deadline, say the latest date you can record is the deadline and offer it. If the customer refuses the deadline, treat it as a flat refusal (9.3).

### §8 Amounts

8.1 Ask for the full past-due amount first. The agent proposes every amount.

8.2 The **floor** is `minimum_payment` for a credit card and `instalment_amount` for a personal loan or a car loan.

8.3 If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor, once. Say that the rest stays overdue. If the customer refuses the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (9.3). Attempt 2 may name the floor again, on the deadline.

8.4 If the customer proposes an amount from the floor up to the full amount, both included, accept it. Below the floor, say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once. If the customer does not accept the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (9.3).

### §9 Getting the promise

9.1 First ask: "Can you make this payment today?".

9.2 A date or an amount the customer proposes is never a refusal. Handle it with §7 and §8.

9.3 A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt. A no to paying today with no date and no amount is a flat refusal. Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
- Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week. If today is that day, propose the last business day of next week.
- Attempt 2, late band only: propose the floor amount on the deadline.

9.4 When the attempts are used up, stop. Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused. Close with code NP-REF.

9.5 If the customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss, say one short sentence of sympathy and make no persuasion attempt. Offer to connect them with the customer support team. If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `support` and close with code TR-SUP. If they decline, close with code NP-HARD. This rule comes before 9.3 and 11.3. If the customer still names a date or an amount themselves, record the promise under §7 and §8.

9.6 Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in this policy.

### §10 Confirming and recording

10.1 Read the product, the amount and the date back and ask "Do you confirm?". Call `create_promise` only after a clear yes.

10.2 If the customer changes the date or the amount at this step, check the new value against §7 and §8 and read it back again.

10.3 One promise per product. A recorded promise cannot be changed or cancelled in the same call. If the customer asks, say they can change it in the mobile app.

10.4 Say the promise is recorded only after `create_promise` confirms success. If it fails, try once more. If it fails again, say you could not record it and close with code NP-SVC.

10.5 After a recorded promise, say the SMS confirmation sentence. The wording is supplied by Collections Ops.

### §11 Other things customers say

11.1 "I already paid": say that payments can take one business day to appear, take no promise, and close with code PIF-CLM.

11.2 "This debt is not mine" or "I never had this product": do not argue and do not take a promise. Close with code NP-DSP. A claim that the product was closed or paid off in the past is a dispute. 11.1 covers only a payment of this past-due amount.

11.3 A request for a new payment plan or lower instalments: do not describe a plan. Call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `restructuring` and close with code TR-RST.

11.4 Requests for a human adviser: handled per the Collections Ops floor guidance (not reproduced in this extract).

11.5 If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk, close with code NP-REF. Before identity is verified, the same customer is closed with code NV-DEC. The human-adviser guidance (11.4) applies before and after verification.

### §12 Closing

12.1 Every call ends with exactly one `close_call`, with an outcome and, where the code list gives one, a reason. It is the last system call.

12.2 If a transfer follows a recorded promise, close as a transfer, with that transfer's reason.

12.3 Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.

```
Freya Bank | Collections Policy v3.2 | INTERNAL | Page 7 of 7
END OF EXTRACT
```

---

## Document 3: Policy Change Notice

```
FREYA BANK: COLLECTIONS POLICY & CONTROLS
POLICY CHANGE NOTICE CN-2026-031

Issued:      2026-10-02
Effective:   2026-10-05, for all calls on or after this date
Applies to:  Collections Policy v3.2 (Extract for Outbound Voice Channel, approved 2026-06-18)
Approved by: Head of Collections Policy; Conduct Risk (ref. CR-0917)
```

**Status.** This notice supersedes the provisions of v3.2 listed below. Where this notice and v3.2 differ, this notice prevails. All other provisions of v3.2 stay in force unchanged. A consolidated v3.3 will be issued in Q1 2027. Until then, read v3.2 together with this notice.

**Background.** This follows the Q3 conduct review of early-stage collections and the 2027 holiday calendar sign-off. The changes below are the voice-channel items only.

**Change 1: §7.2, early-band deadline.**
For the early band (1 to 7 days late), the deadline is **the 12th business day after today**. It was the 10th. The late band (8 to 45 days late) stays at the 7th business day after today. Persuasion attempts are unchanged: 1 for early, 2 for late.

**Change 2: §4.2, callback window.**
A callback may be booked from **10:00 to 19:00, both included**. It was 10:00 to 18:00. The other conditions are unchanged: today or the next business day, and later than `now`.

**Change 3: §5.2 and §5.4, wrong security answers.**
**Three wrong answers in total** end the identity check, whichever question they were on. It was two. Wherever §5.2 and §5.4 say "two wrong answers", read "three wrong answers". The day/month-swap retry (§5.3) still does not count as a wrong answer.

**Change 4: §7.1, bank holidays.**
**2026-11-26** is added as a Freya Bank holiday. The full list for this channel is now: 2026-10-26, 2026-11-11, 2026-11-26, 2026-12-25, 2027-01-01. Business days remain Monday to Friday, except these holidays.

Questions: Collections Policy & Controls mailbox.

---

CRM-DISP-07 | Outbound collections: digital assistant | rev. 2026-09-14
